neighbours.label: Role/occupation person nouns naming a kind of person (learner, worker, teacher, student, member, soldier, researcher, musician), esp. right after 'the' or as a compound modifier
fire: Last spring the district hired a new science teacher who had previously worked in a research lab.
Union leaders argued that every factory worker deserves paid sick leave and a safe workplace.
Among the nursing home residents, the oldest living member of the choir still sings on Sundays.
A good language learner keeps a notebook of new phrases and reviews it each evening.
Reporters interviewed a retired soldier who had served in three different campaigns overseas.
The journal published a survey of graduate student attitudes toward remote supervision.
At the museum, a young researcher showed visitors how the old printing press once operated.
Everyone in the village knew the baker, but the shy musician who lived above the shop was a mystery.
quiet: Last spring the district approved a new science curriculum that had previously been piloted in a research lab.
Union leaders argued that every factory floor deserves clean air conditioning and a safe layout.
Among the nursing home residents, the oldest living tradition of the choir is still sung on Sundays.
A good language course keeps a glossary of new phrases and reviews it each evening.
Reporters examined a retired warship that had served in three different campaigns overseas.
The journal published a survey of graduate program funding and its effect on remote supervision.
At the museum, a large printing press showed visitors how the old newspaper once operated.
Everyone in the village knew the bakery, but the quiet attic that lay above the shop was a mystery.

notes: 10x pilot (concept-maps/tenx, census arm): label and 16 sentences written by a fresh Sonnet 5.5 subagent from a packet (card + all-pole band samples + concept-census evidence (which concepts and domains selected the pole)); no probes. An Opus gate checked rule-level items only (8 + 8, 0 overlap with census and probe text, near misses free of the declared trigger) and edited nothing. Labeller's note: Strong activations are singular agent/occupation nouns (learner, worker, teacher, student, member, soldier), often following 'the' or inside a title/modifier; band samples show the same for researcher, musician, scientist, person. Pole is broad (1.5% of tokens), so near misses use non-person nouns in matching frames.
